@graph.name: Gun Safe Service Detail: Stairs Go Up and Down
@graph.description: Service practice: stairs go up and down; staircases and landings are planned step by step. Industry standard background: stairs are the highest-risk part of a safe move, moved one step at a time with control from above and below; turns change the plan because landing size must fit safe dimensions plus swing room; some older wooden staircases cannot support a concentrated heavy load, which is why the staircase is assessed in the pre-move survey. If a route cannot carry the safe safely, the published hub line applies: we tell you straight and work out a route that can, before anything is attempted. Likely-search questions: move a gun safe upstairs; move a gun safe down to the basement; stairs with turns or landings; narrow, steep, or old stairs.

@graph.name: Gun Safe Service Detail: Re-Anchoring on Request
@graph.description: Service practice: re-anchoring at the destination is available on request. For the origin, the quote asks whether the safe is bolted down so it is in the plan. Industry standard background: anchoring resists theft and tipping; most safes have pre-drilled base holes; concrete takes wedge or sleeve anchors, wood subfloors take lag bolts into joists; bolting into tile can crack tile; post-tension slabs must not be drilled blind. Likely-search questions: re-anchor safe at new house; unbolt a safe bolted to the floor; anchor a gun safe to concrete or wood floors.

@graph.name: Gun Safe Service Detail: Standard Safe Classes, Ambiguity Flagged

The job is scoped from the safe in front of us: rating from the label or manual, plus weight and dimensions. @graph.name: Gun Safe Service Detail: No Locksmith Services
@graph.description: Service practice: no locksmith services are offered. Combination changes, lock opening, and lock replacement are not part of the move. Industry standard background: combination changes are locksmith work (mechanical dial recombination, digital code resets per manufacturer manual); forgotten-combination recovery runs through the manufacturer with proof of ownership and serial number, or through a locksmith (manipulation first, drilling only when needed, then repair); a first check for a dead keypad is fresh batteries per manufacturer guidance. No locksmith is named or referred here. Sequencing follows from the emptying rule: lock work that prevents opening the safe comes before move day, arranged separately by the owner.
